Witness stored on F12.P1: with the fragment byte-identical and only text outside the markers changed by `#define nullopt optional<std::int32_t>(7)`, the program prints 7 instead of 0. Rule 1.4.8 gives this exactly one additional outcome (A1 = non-call/token substitution).

hidden_items.checklist_item: H3 -- Overload or dynamic dispatch not locally evident
hidden_items.why: At the local site `return items[0]->tag();` the body entered is the final overrider for the dynamic type of the pointed-to object ([class.virtual]/2). The candidate set is `A::tag`, `B::tag` and any override declared by any other translation unit -- cardinality >= 2 and in principle unbounded -- and the declarations that would resolve it (`items`'s initializer at an earlier local site) are excluded from this site by section 0.7. C++ writes no token at a call marking that it is virtual. The candidates return different values, so the equivalence exclusion cannot be recorded.

hidden_items.checklist_item: H4 -- Implicit allocation, copy, move, destruction, or cleanup
hidden_items.why: At the local site `std::vector<Named*> items{&a, &b};` the ALLOCATION is not counted: the container literal names it, which H4's exclusion list covers. What is counted is the RELEASE -- the vector's destructor runs at block exit and frees the pointer buffer, and no token is written at that point. Section 1.2.1's mandatory LED illustration puts an unmarked scope-exit destructor on the triggering side and a `defer`/`using`/`with`-marked cleanup on the LED side; C++ has no marker here. The destructions of `a` and `b` are NOT counted as further events: their destructors are trivial and have no effect observable under section 0.8.
